metadata.title: Nobody Wrote This.
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Merhaba (Turkish), one word — fresh for this channel (Namaste, Kumusta, Sawubona and Hej are already spent on the four prior reels). Narrator is Yatra on her OWN channel (@Yatra), so IN-FOR-BEAR LAW does not apply and no 'in for Bear' sign-off appears. Voice: Kokoro af_bella ('Bella').
metadata.color_semantics: Fidelity claude palette. ONE terracotta #D97757 event per beat, and it always marks THE MACHINE-WRITTEN SHARE — the thing being measured. The accent carries the finding rather than decorating the frame; citations are always muted ink, never accent, because provenance is not emphasis.
metadata.note: ILLUSTRATE LAW: the Claude UI appears at B00 (cold open, with RESULT lines), B04 (the ask micro-beat of the one ask→result pair, resolved by B05), B11 (verdict artifact), B12 (handoff), B13 (outro). Every other beat illustrates its concept with a purpose-built Remotion scene. HONESTY: every figure on screen was supplied verbatim by the human and carries its citation in the frame; no figure is derived, and the human-written share of LinkedIn posts is deliberately NOT rendered even though it is arithmetically available — see FACTCHECK.md.

beats.narration_text: Merhaba. If LinkedIn has felt strange to read lately — every post the same shape, the same cadence — you are not imagining it. Somebody counted a million posts. LinkedIn came out worst.

show.event: Cream page, serif greeting 'Merhaba, Yatra' above the composer
The ask types itself in, line by line
Terracotta send button arms — the ONE accent of the beat
Three result lines stagger in — the ask lands ANSWERED, per COLD OPEN LAW

props.command: How much of what I read on LinkedIn is actually written by AI? Give me measured numbers across platforms, not vibes — and tell me whether people are lightly editing with AI or handing the whole post over.
output: 41% of long-form LinkedIn posts are fully AI-generated
the highest share of any platform in the study
and it is all-or-nothing — almost nobody edits

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole thing in one breath. The platform people use to look professional is now the most machine-written place measured. Not lightly assisted. Written for them.

show.event: First clause sets in serif, ink, left-aligned in the safe box
'the most machine-written place measured' lands in terracotta as it is spoken
'Not lightly assisted.' types in beneath, then is struck through
'Written for them.' replaces it — the reframe enacted, not described
Rule draws left-to-right under the statement and holds

beats.narration_text: The comparison deserves to be drawn properly, so I asked for it — every platform in the scan, sorted, average marked.

show.event: Composer returns; the generation prompt types itself in — the ACTUAL ask behind the next beat's graphic
Terracotta send arms

props.command: Chart all five platforms from the scan side by side, sorted high to low, values printed verbatim with their ranges intact, and mark the cross-platform average as a reference line.

beats.narration_text: And the gap is the story. LinkedIn, forty-one percent. Medium, about thirty-one. X, twenty-five to twenty-nine. Substack, ten. Reddit, as low as four. Across all five platforms, the rate is one in four.

beats.narration_text: Remember the middle bin — write with a machine, then edit? On LinkedIn, four point three percent. Basically empty. People are not polishing. They are handing the post over whole.

show.event: B02's three bins return, empty — the callback the narration explicitly asks for

beats.narration_text: Here is the structural joke. LinkedIn ships a button called Enhance Post that writes for you. LinkedIn also downranks AI content. The same company builds the faucet and reports the flood.

show.event: Left block sets: 'Enhance Post' — an AI writing tool, shipped in the product; its arrow drives RIGHT
Right block sets: 'Downranks AI-generated content'; its arrow drives LEFT
The two arrowheads meet in the middle and stall — the collision IS the argument
The collision point flares terracotta and the label 'same platform' prints between them
Citation holds beneath

beats.narration_text: Where could this be wrong? Detection is a probability, not a confession. But Substack and Reddit sit at the bottom of the same scan. So this is not AI. This is LinkedIn.

show.event: First stress test sets with its terracotta marker: detection is probabilistic
Second sets: the same method produced ~10% and 4–13% elsewhere
Third sets: what would actually falsify the read
Closer lands in serif: saturation is a platform choice

data.title: Where this could be wrong

items.label: Detection is a probability, not a confession
items.why: a classifier estimates; it does not read intent, and no accuracy figure was published here

items.label: The same scan found Substack at ~10% and Reddit as low as 4%
items.why: if the method inflated everything, the floor would not be that low

items.label: What would falsify it
items.why: a rescan where LinkedIn's assisted middle is large — that would make this editing, not outsourcing

data.closer: Saturation is a platform choice, not a law of nature.

beats.narration_text: Two things follow. If you are building a personal brand there, the medium is now suspected by default — my read, not a finding. And since August second, Article Fifty requires disclosure.

Both blocks settle onto the axis and hold

data.note: One of these is my opinion. The other one has a date.

beats.narration_text: The verdict. One — LinkedIn is the most AI-saturated platform measured. Two — it is all-or-nothing; the assisted middle is four point three percent. Three — the platform sells the tool and penalises the output. If you actually write, that is now an advantage.

artifactLines: LinkedIn is the most AI-saturated major platform measured: 41% of long-form posts (250+ words) fully AI-generated (Pangram Labs, "AI in Your Feed," July 2026).
It is all-or-nothing: only 4.3% of posts are AI-assisted/mixed — people outsource the whole post rather than edit (Pangram Labs / Tech Times).
One third of the ~1M posts scanned, but nearly 62% of all AI content detected — and the platform ships "Enhance Post" while downranking AI output (Pangram Labs).
EU AI Act Article 50 disclosure rules took effect August 2, 2026 (Tech Times). If you actually write, that is now an advantage.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: take my last ten LinkedIn posts, and for each, tell me which parts only I could have written — a number, a name, something that went wrong — and which parts any model would produce. Then rewrite the weakest using only what is unrepeatable. Look for whether it points at facts, not adjectives.

show.event: Serif 'Your turn.' replaces the persona greeting — the one persona-less greeting
The prompt types itself in as the narration reads it aloud, verbatim
Terracotta send arms
Three-item rubric stacks in as each check is discussed — the scaffolded task

props.command: Take my last 10 LinkedIn posts. For each, tell me which parts only I could have written — a specific number, a name, something that went wrong — and which parts any model would produce from the same prompt. Then rewrite the weakest one using only what is unrepeatable.
output: grade it: does it point at facts only you have?
grade it: does it cut the lines any model could write?
grade it: is the rewrite shorter AND more specific?
